headline: Seasonal Entry Permits for Canada's Second Oldest Provincial Park
reservation: Day-use vehicle permits are required and can be booked in advance via the Ontario Parks reservation portal. Camping reservations are highly competitive for the summer months and should be secured as early as the five-month rolling window allows.

days.title: Old Growth Forest and History

stops.name: Tulip Tree Trail
stops.detail: Walk the barrier-free boardwalk through a rare Carolinian forest featuring massive tulip trees and diverse flora.

stops.name: Rondeau Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Explore exhibits detailing the natural history of the sandspit and the park's establishment in the late 1800s.

days.driving: Allow 15–25 minutes from Blenheim to the park interior; roads are flat and well-marked.
days.note: Biting insects can be prevalent in the forest during early summer; seasonal conditions vary.

days.title: Bay-Side Exploration

stops.name: Marsh Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or walk this 7-kilometer linear trail along the edge of Rondeau Bay to spot turtles and waterfowl.

stops.name: South Point Trail
stops.detail: Observe the ongoing coastal erosion and landform changes at the southern tip of the peninsula.

days.driving: Short drives between trailheads; bike rentals may be available seasonally within the park.
days.note: The Marsh Trail is exposed to sun and wind; check weather forecasts for Lake Erie carefully.

days.title: Lake Erie Shoreline
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Beach Access Area

stops.name: Black Oak Trail
stops.detail: Meander through a savannah habitat that supports a unique community of plants and rare butterflies.

stops.name: Main Beach
stops.detail: Spend the afternoon on the 11-kilometer sandy beach on the eastern side of the park.

days.driving: Minimal travel on the park's main loop road; allow time for finding parking near popular beach access points.
days.note: Water currents in Lake Erie can be strong; swim only in designated areas and observe safety flags.

intel.title: Beachfront Logistics
intel.text: Parking lots are distributed along the main road near beach access points. During the spring birding festival, the Visitor Centre lot fills very quickly.

intel.title: Regional Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong throughout the park due to the flat topography and proximity to Chatham-Kent. Remote corners of the Marsh Trail may have weaker data speeds.

intel.title: Blenheim Gateway
intel.text: Blenheim is the nearest town for fuel and major grocery runs. Ensure your tank is sufficient for park exploration as there are no stations within the gates.

intel.title: Birding Peak
intel.text: May is the busiest time for birdwatchers seeking warblers. Suggested arrival is before 8 AM during the Festival of Flight to secure access to guided walks.

intel.title: Private Cottages
intel.text: The park contains a community of private cottages; visitors must respect private property boundaries and stick to official park trails and roads.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Windsor International Airport, then drive east for approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes. Check in at the park gatehouse for your permit.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are ideal for the paved loops; the park is also highly navigable by bicycle due to its flat terrain.
plan.goldenHour: Rondeau Bay for sunset; the calm waters on the western side of the peninsula offer clear views across the marsh.
